prompt: The blog is plain files that are the same for everyone, so any simple host can serve it.
why: Pages that are identical for every visitor are static.
trap: They may be cached, but the clue is that they never change per visitor.

prompt: Your account page shows your own name and orders, built when you request it.
why: A page made fresh for each visitor is dynamic.
trap: Cookies identify you, but the page being built per request is the clue.

prompt: The docs site is turned into HTML files ahead of time, before anyone visits.
tells: turned into HTML files ahead of time
why: Building pages ahead of time produces static pages.
trap: It isn't a cached copy of a dynamic page; it's made static from the start.

prompt: The news feed is different for every user and changes each time it's opened.
why: Content that depends on who's asking and when is dynamic.
trap: Sessions say who you are; the page being per-user is dynamic.

prompt: A portfolio site costs almost nothing to host because there's no server code, just files.
trap: Cheap because nothing is computed per request.

prompt: Search results pages are generated from the database for each query.
tells: generated from the database for each query
why: Pages generated per request are dynamic, even if they use a database.
trap: The database is the source; the page itself is dynamic.
